subject: Geolocation of data, retention windows, and pseudonymization options

Subject: Data residency/retention — PHI handling questions

Hi Karthik,

Quick intro — I lead InfoSec at MedLogic. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will include PHI (EHR excerpts, hashed identifiers). Before we move to a formal security review, we need high-level answers so our legal and procurement teams can scope requirements: 

1) Residency: can all stored data (request logs, KV cache, model context) be pinned to US-only regions (and contractually enforced)?
2) Retention: what are the default retention windows for token-level logs, raw request/response payloads, and aggregated metrics? Can retention be shortened to 0 (no storage) for specific tenants?
3) Deletion guarantees: when a customer requests erasure, what is the timeline and evidence we can get that data (including backups and snapshots) was removed?
4) Redaction & pseudonymization: do you support server-side automatic PHI redaction, field-level pseudonymization/hashing, or do you recommend client-side masking? Any reference playbooks or sample SLA language would be helpful.

If you can send a short summary and any relevant playbooks (non-legal, technical operational), that would be great. We may need a 30-minute sync after that.

Thanks,
Emma Watson
Senior InfoSec Manager
MedLogic Health

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (Customer Security) and Naomi (Data Lifecycle) to provide the technical playbook and an operational view. High-level answers below; Naomi will follow with specifics and a short playbook PDF.

Summary answers (top-line):
- Residency: Yes — for Hosted accounts we offer region pinning to US regions (contractual). For regulated customers we can provide Dedicated or Private deployments that keep control plane and data inside customer VPCs.
- Retention: Default hosted telemetry is conservative (we keep request logs for operational troubleshooting; default token-level logs: 30 days). Important: these are configurable at the account level — enterprise agreements can set shorter windows or opt for "no retention" for request/response payloads. Aggregated metrics/usage summaries are retained longer by default (up to 365 days) but can also be scoped down.
- Deletion guarantees: We run a documented 3-phase erasure workflow (mark, purge caches/backups, audit). Typical completion: primary store purge within 72 hours, backups/snapshot purge within 30–90 days depending on backup cycle (we provide audit evidence). Naomi will paste recommended SLA language.
- Redaction & pseudonymization: Options include client-side masking (recommended for highest control), Redwood server-side redaction (pattern-based redactors + ML-assisted PHI detector), and tokenization/pseudonymization via field-level hashing. For PHI workloads we often recommend combining client-side pre-mask with server-side tokenization for analytics.

Attached: redaction-playbook-v2.pdf (technical playbook), medlogic-map-terms.docx (starter contract language).

Would you like a 30-minute call later this week (Wed/Thu)? If you share preferred times I can send a calendar invite.

— Karthik

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency/retention — PHI handling questions

Karthik / Monica — adding a few operational details you can share with MedLogic. Paste below is a short-form playbook excerpt; full PDF attached in Karthik's message.

Operational erasure workflow (summary):
1) Receipt and validation — customer submits erasure via support portal or API (we capture request id).
2) Mark stage — records matching selector (customer_id, conversation_id, hashed_id) are flagged in primary index; real-time serving routed to avoid stale cache hits.
3) Primary data purge — delete objects from primary store and KV caches (completion target: 72 hours).
4) Backup & snapshot purge — deletes scheduled at next snapshot window; final purge completed within 30–90 days depending on backup retention policy for that deployment.
5) Audit evidence — we produce a deletion report (object ids + deletion timestamp + operation id) and sign it with HSM-backed key (customer can request hashed attestations).

Notes on redaction and pseudonymization:
- Client-side masking: recommended when customers must retain no plaintext PHI in any third-party system. We provide SDK hooks and patterns for deterministic hashing when customers want stable pseudonyms.
- Server-side redaction: pattern-driven scrubbing (SSNs, MRNs, DOBs) + optional ML classifier for context-sensitive PHI. Server redaction can be configured to either replace with tokens (e.g., <PHI_HASH:abcd1234>) or remove fields entirely.
- Pseudonymization design patterns: (a) salt + HMAC of identifying fields where salt is customer-managed (recommended), (b) Redwood-managed HSM salt with limited retrieval (alternate). For regulated customers we advise customer-managed keys (KMS) to minimize exposure.

Suggested SLA snippet you can include in the contract: 
"Upon receipt of a validated erasure request, Redwood will complete primary data deletion within 72 hours and initiate backup/snapshot purging; final removal from backup systems will be completed within 90 days. Redwood will provide an auditable deletion report signed with a customer-requested key."

Operational caveats:
- Hosted accounts: default telemetry retention is 30 days; choosing zero retention disables request/response logging but may limit supportability.
- Dedicated/Private: retention and deletion policies are customer-configurable; on-prem installs can be configured to meet local retention requirements.

Attachments in the playbook: step-by-step API examples (POST /v1/erasures), recommended selectors, and a template deletion attestation. I'll extract the API snippet for the customer if you want.

— Naomi
Senior Product Manager, Data Lifecycle
Redwood Inference
